title: Potential, Potential Difference & Potential Energy — Interactive Concept Map
topicTitle: Potential, Potential Difference and Potential Energy — Mindmap and Conceptual Hierarchy
notes: Comprehensive conceptual breakdown of electrostatic potential, potential difference, potential energy, equipotential surfaces, and potential gradient.
Covers core NEB formulas: V = -∫E·dr, V = kQ/r, E = -∇V, U = kq₁q₂/r, and 1 eV = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.
Unifies the electrostatics chain: field lines → equipotential surfaces (perpendicular) → potential gradient (E = -dV/dx) → potential energy (ΔU = -W).

subtopics.name: Definition & Properties
points: V = W/q₀ = -∫_∞^P E·dr (SI unit: volt, 1 V = 1 J/C)
Scalar, path-independent (conservative field: ∮E·dr = 0)
ΔV = V_B - V_A = -∫_A^B E·dr (can be positive or negative)
Dimensional formula: [M L² T⁻³ I⁻¹]
Reference level fixed by convention: V(∞) = 0

subtopics.name: Potential of Standard Distributions
points: Point charge: V = kQ/r (falls as 1/r, field falls as 1/r²)
Line charge: V = -(λ / 2πε₀) ln(r/r₀)
Infinite plane sheet: V = -(σ / 2ε₀)x (uniform field ⇒ linear V)
Charged shell: V = kQ/r outside; constant kQ/R inside
Superposition: V = k Σ qᵢ / rᵢ (algebraic, scalar sum)

subtopics.name: Gradient Relation
points: E = -dV/dx (uniform field along one axis)
Vector form: E = -∇V with ∇ = î ∂/∂x + ĵ ∂/∂y + k̂ ∂/∂z
Field points toward steepest DECREASE of potential
Differentiate V = kQ/r to recover E = kQ/r²

subtopics.name: Graphical Interpretation
points: Slope of V–r graph = -(potential gradient) = -E
Straight line ⇒ uniform field; hyperbola ⇒ point charge; log curve ⇒ line charge
Steep graph segment ⇒ strong field; flat segment ⇒ weak field

subtopics.name: Core Properties
points: Surface of constant V: ΔV = 0, so W = qΔV = 0 (no work done)
Always perpendicular to electric field lines (dV = -E·dl = 0 forces θ = 90°)
Two equipotential surfaces can never intersect
Close spacing ⇒ strong field; wide spacing ⇒ weak field
Conductor in equilibrium = single equipotential surface

subtopics.name: Shapes for Standard Configurations
points: Point charge → concentric spheres
Line charge → coaxial cylinders
Infinite plane sheet → parallel planes, uniformly spaced
Conducting shell → sphere (V = kQ/R) plus constant-potential interior cavity

subtopics.name: Potential Energy
points: U = qV = k q₁ q₂ / r for two charges
Like charges: U > 0 (repulsive, unbound); unlike charges: U < 0 (attractive, bound)
Multiple charges: U = k Σ_{i<j} qᵢ qⱼ / rᵢⱼ (count each pair once)
ΔU = -W_electric (force always acts to reduce U)

subtopics.name: Electron Volt
points: 1 eV = e × 1 V = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ J (an ENERGY unit)
1 keV = 10³ eV (X-rays); 1 MeV = 10⁶ eV (nuclear binding)
1 GeV = 10⁹ eV (particle colliders)
